g.text: gasket inside edge flush with R280, no step > 0.3
ring 108: fillet 4 all round to the shell outside,

svg.text: 1. Why bolted: both shaft ends pass through the end plates and the ribbons run 15 [.59] from the plates, so a welded-both-ends trough could not take the
agitator. With 110 off, the agitator slides in from the free end.
2. Ring 108 is welded to the shell outside with its face flush with the shell end, then the face is skimmed flat (0.2) on the mill or with a flange
3. The free-end plate and its box (104) are welded as a sub-weldment (W3) before the trough weldment is aligned with the bar.
4. Gasket: cut from 3 mm FDA silicone with the DXF; replace at every agitator removal. Torque H13 in a cross pattern 10 then 25 N·m.
5. Dowel option: 2 x Ø8 dowels at 3 and 9 o'clock (ring + plate drilled together) to keep the box concentric after removal.
